structured_result.summary:
All three earlier P3 problems are fixed, and the fixes don't change which values are accepted.

- **Startup errors:** they now name both TOSI_* and the legacy TASK_RUNNERS_* variable. This includes the bare ParseIntError case, which now maps to the "must contain a valid number" message. The accept/reject rules in config::var are unchanged.
- **Invalid-value test:** for empty and "invalid" values it now checks for the exact message. That proves the failure happens at the intended check and doesn't fall back to the legacy value.
- **Doctor test:** it now runs both backends three ways — no marker, TOSI_CHILD=1 and TASK_RUNNERS_CHILD=1 — after clearing both markers from the inherited environment. Each run must exit successfully with ready=true.
- **README:** it now gives each host's commands to remove the old plugin and its catalog registration.
- **Plugin subtitle:** shortened to 26 characters, and the package test now asserts it is 30 characters or fewer.
- **Cargo.lock:** the diff only moves the tosi package entry earlier in the file; the other entries are the same text in a new position.

One minor issue remains: the README migration steps tell users to install tosi before removing the stale task-runners catalog. You've already seen Codex marketplace commands fail with the stale catalog, so that order may not work.

findings.title: Migration steps install the new plugin before removing the stale catalog
findings.scenario: After the source directory moves, a user follows the README in order. They run `codex plugin marketplace add` and `codex plugin add tosi@tosi-local` while task-runners-local is still registered and points at the deleted task-runners path. Only then do they run the removal commands at lines 120-123.
findings.evidence: README.md:114-117 says to "Install `tosi@tosi-local` ... then remove the old plugin and its catalog registration". You reported that `codex marketplace list` already fails because of the stale original directory. I can't see from this snapshot whether `marketplace add` or `plugin add` fail the same way.
findings.impact: If Codex catalog operations check every registered catalog, the documented first step can fail on both machines before the cleanup commands are reached. Even if it succeeds, there is a short window where both plugins are installed.
findings.suggested_correction: Put the removal block first: remove task-runners@task-runners-local, then remove the task-runners-local catalog (both hosts), then add tosi-local and install tosi@tosi-local. The old installation is already broken once the directory moves, so removing it first loses nothing; Claude's `--keep-data` still keeps its plugin data. Alternatively, keep the current order if your actual migration shows it works on both hosts.

coverage: All of FIXES.diff: Cargo.lock, README.md, src/main.rs, tests/diagnostics.rs, tests/shutdown.rs, xtask/src/main.rs
Final src/main.rs error paths and config.rs precedence (unchanged): acceptance rules are the same, and both names now appear in all three configuration errors
Checked that each test's expected message matches the actual main.rs text for DEFAULT_BACKEND and MAX_CONCURRENCY with empty and invalid values
The doctor test runs with no marker, TOSI_CHILD=1 and TASK_RUNNERS_CHILD=1 for both backends, after clearing both markers from the inherited environment
Plugin subtitle length (26 characters) and the new package assertion of 30 or fewer
Cargo.lock diff: only the position of the tosi package entry changed; the moved entries are identical
limitations: This was a source-only follow-up: no tests, builds or host commands were run. Pass/fail results come from your validation.

I could not check the README's host CLI commands and flags (`codex plugin remove`, `codex plugin marketplace remove`, `claude plugin uninstall --scope user --keep-data`, `claude plugin marketplace remove --scope user`) against the installed host versions without running them.
I couldn't tell from source whether the stale catalog blocks `codex plugin marketplace add` or `plugin add`; the ordering finding depends on that.
I did not confirm the snapshot's SHA-256 myself.
The regenerated package, installed-plugin checks and paid live-provider runs are still pending, and this review doesn't cover them. The end-to-end live-gating test gap remains, as you documented.
